content.content:
15:The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the harness does is streamed back as it happens. A task's run takes its prompt as a stream of messages rather than a single one, so it can be fed more while it works, as its feeding says.
20:The harness in use is the one picked in the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope): Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked. It is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, not for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks, the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another harness starts a new one.
21:Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage, and result, whichever harness wrote it:
43:A message reaches the harness when it finishes what it is doing rather than interrupting it, so a run that is mid-tool-call takes it once that call is over. The harness echoes each message back as it takes it in, with `--replay-user-messages`. A message taken in between turns is answered with a result of its own, and one taken while a turn is under way is answered within that turn, sharing its result. A result no longer ends the task on its own: the run ends with a result once every message sent has been taken in, at which point its input is closed and the task finishes, in the state of that last result. A run that is stopped closes its input straight away.
44:Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.
49:Images attached to a prompt, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, are given to the harness as it takes them: to Claude Code as image content blocks, base64-encoded with their media type, in the same stream-json user message as the prompt's text, after it; to Codex with an `--image` argument per image; and to OpenCode with a `--file` argument per image. A message fed to a running Claude Code task carries its images the same way, and a Claude Code run that isn't fed more but has images is given its prompt as a stream-json message too, so the images can go with it. Codex's options end with `--` before the prompt when it is given images. Questions take images as tasks do.
53:The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Tasks share one ongoing conversation, and each task sent carries it on. A task that starts while a task of the other lane is running, as the [PromptSendingScope](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) lets it, carries on a copy of that conversation as it was when it started, as a question does, so tasks running at the same time never write over each other; the conversation tasks carry on afterwards is that of whichever task finished most recently. When the project is opened, tasks carry on the latest conversation in its history. Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background, and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
54:A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says: the next request starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after its tasks' or questions' conversation was left starts a new one too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.

content.text:
Send this in **Chain** mode:

```text
A task must not show as finished while work its run started in the background
is still going. Right now a Claude Code task that starts a shell command in
the background (run_in_background, e.g. a long `cargo build`) and then ends
its turn to wait for it is marked finished: Claude Code emits a `result` when
the turn ends, and the harness takes that result as the last one, because the
only background work it waits on is subagents (`task_started` with
`task_type: local_agent`). The task closes, its input is closed so it can't be
fed more, and the build carries on unseen. When the build ends, the harness
would have woken the agent to act on it, but the task is already over.

What should be true afterwards:

1. Background work of any kind holds the run open. The run keeps the set of
   Claude Code background tasks that have started and not yet ended, whatever
   their task_type (local_agent, local_bash, or any kind added later):
   `system` `task_started` adds its task_id, and `task_notification` for that
   id removes it, whatever its status. `task_notification` doesn't say its
   kind, so ids are matched against those seen starting.

2. A result only ends the run once every message sent has been taken in AND
   no background task is still going. A result that comes while any is still
   going is an answer (Answered, as a result is today while a subagent is
   running): the task stays running, its input stays open, and it can still
   be fed. The run ends on the first result after the last background task
   has ended.

3. The Subagents panel is unchanged: it still lists only local_agent tasks.
   Background shell tasks hold the run open but aren't shown as subagents.

4. A task isn't shown as finished until the harness process has exited as
   well as having given its last result. If a last result has come but the
   process is still running, the task stays running until it exits, then
   finishes in the state of that last result. A process that exits with no
   result finishes as it does today.

5. Stopping a task still ends it straight away, background work and all
   (its whole process group is killed), whatever is still running.

Spec: the rule for when a run ends is in the harness-integration scope's
feeding paragraph ("A result no longer ends the task on its own: the run ends
with a result once every message sent has been taken in ..."), and the
subagents rule in the right sidebar's subagents component. Update those rather
than adding parallel anchors, and make the harness-integration scope say that
background tasks of every kind, not only subagents, hold the run open.

Code: src/harness.rs — Messages (rename `subagents` to something like
`background`, holding every started task id), Messages::read, Feed::read
(input closed only on the real last result), and the run loop / Stop::wait,
so the task finishes on process exit after the last result. subagent_event
stays as it is for the panel. Update the tests: the existing one that says a
background shell starts no subagent should still pass, and add tests that a
result while a local_bash task is running is Answered and keeps input open,
that the result after its task_notification is Finished, and that a task
whose last result has come doesn't finish until its process exits.
```

This only fixes Claude Code runs. Codex and OpenCode already finish on process exit and don't report background tasks this way.
